reasoning: Recent, reputable polling and forecast data for New Hampshire’s 2026 Senate race consistently show Democrat Chris Pappas holding a mid‑single‑digit lead over Republican John Sununu, with multiple polls in June and July indicating a margin in the D+3 to D+7 range and an aggregated polling average around D+5–6.[1][2][3][9][11][12] There is no new general‑election presidential polling for New Hampshire in the last 45 days from major outlets, so the best current quantified margin applies to the Senate race, which can reasonably be characterized as approximately **D+5** at the moment.[1][2][3][9][11][12] New Hampshire’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is **D+1**, indicating only a slight structural Democratic lean.[1]

sources.name: UNH Survey Center via Eciks.org summary
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll found Chris Pappas leading John Sununu 47% to 44% in the New Hampshire Senate race, a D+3 margin in a statistical tie.

sources.name: Peak Insights poll via NRSC release
sources.details: NRSC‑released Peak Insights poll showed Pappas at 43% and Sununu at 42%, a D+1 margin within the margin of error, indicating a nearly tied Senate race.

sources.name: PollsMax New Hampshire 2026 Senate Forecast
sources.details: State-specific polling aggregation for the New Hampshire Senate race reports a polling average of 47.3% for the Democrat and 41.9% for the Republican, a D+5.4 margin.

sources.details: Forecast model using recent public polls (Saint Anselm D+3, Emerson D+2) gives Democrats an 83% chance to win the New Hampshire Senate race, implying a modest but consistent Democratic edge.
sources.date_range: March 16-18 and March 21-23, 2026 (public polling basis for current forecast, last updated June 30, 2026)

sources.details: State political newsletter’s polling average for the Pappas–Sununu Senate general election shows Pappas at 47.2% and Sununu at 41.7%, a D+5.5 margin.
sources.date_range: Through late June 2026 (citing UNH, Emerson, Saint Anselm polls)

sources.details: UNH election polling reported Chris Pappas leading Sununu by 3 points in the open U.S. Senate race, reinforcing a small but persistent Democratic advantage.
